doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Titles as memory, the present moment and fantasy; literature
summary: She says her instrumental pieces reflect childhood memories, the present moment (paddleboarding) or imagination, and mentions her love of American literature such as Jonathan Franzen.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I love it. Are you familiar with the American Entertainer Steve Allen?
Yes. My mother used to listen to him.
Okay. Because I asked him a question about naming instrumental compositions and he could be pithy and a bit sarcastic and he said basically well instrumental music can’t tell you anything.
But you’re saying that you write music without lyrics that reflects memories that you have.

Yeah it does. It reflects those childhood memories of innocence a lot. I think there’s a point in our lives where the innocent line happens and it breaks and you’re not innocent anymore, and I think a lot like that kind of thing was then. But if I go back to that project, the other piece was completely in the now, which was a piece about me learning how to paddleboard over rapids and I guess there were a lot of currents, so it was just in the now so it was just called “Passing — Passing Machine” is that it? I forget. But something like that. But it was just the area I was in and the moment I’m in. So sometimes I capture just that exact moment I’m in that has nothing to do with my past. Do you know what I mean?

So sometimes I guess I do reflections and sometimes I’m doing — or reflections from childhood and other times I’m doing reflections of something very recent. Or I might be imagining something I’ve never done so there’s no rhyme or reason to titles sometimes. But fantasy is a big part of it for me. I’ll send you my new liner notes of my new album because it’s all about what we’re talking about. And one of the things is that I start my liner notes saying I’ve always had my nose in a book and — or my family always laughed or my family always noticed or something, I forget what I said, about me always having my nose in a book. And so as much as I had this gorgeous supernatural environment around me just like Ingrid did, and I think it comes through in her trumpet and her writing, I think also I was really, I’ve always been very interested in American literature actually, or more current American literature like Jonathan Franzen. I love his
descriptions of society in general so I might just sit and — I’ve written pieces about his books and his place with emotion.
